text: "Faith is the substance of things hoped for." Without hope, faith has nothing to stand under.
explanation:
We often hear that faith is what moves God, and it is; faith is heaven's currency. But read the order: faith is the hupostasis, literally what stands under, of things hoped for. Hope comes first. It's the picture in front of you; faith is the ground under your feet that holds you there.

If you can't imagine yourself healed, free or restored, faith has nothing to give substance to. So let God paint the picture. "Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may abound in hope." See the good future He promises, then stand on it.

text: Suffering produces perseverance, perseverance produces character, and character produces hope, a hope that "does not disappoint."
explanation:
"Having been justified by faith, we have peace with God… through whom also we have access by faith into this grace in which we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God." You're standing on favour ground. Then Paul adds that we glory in tribulations too: not because suffering comes from God, but because of what He produces through it.

The world says, "Don't get your hopes up; you'll only be disappointed." But your hope rests on the cross, where every harvest of sin was reaped in Jesus' body. Nothing waits in your future but good. This hope will never put you to shame.

text: Hope is "an anchor of the soul… which enters behind the veil, where the forerunner has entered for us, even Jesus."
explanation:
A ship that drops anchor still gets hit by storms, but it isn't swept away; the anchor pulls it back. Our anchor isn't on the seabed. It's fastened inside the Holy of Holies, in God's very presence. It's like a ship still in an English harbour with its anchor already fixed in New York: however rough the crossing, it will arrive.

In Paul's day, a forerunner was a servant sent ahead to announce that an important person was coming. Jesus took the forerunner's place. God accepted Him, and so the ones following Him are already accepted. Hold on to that hope. It holds on to you.

text: "Put on… as a helmet, the hope of salvation." When you lose the assurance of your salvation, your mind is left unprotected.
explanation:
As a teenager, one preacher read a book teaching that believers can lose their salvation and believed it. Almost immediately, blasphemous thoughts began flooding his mind, and he became convinced he'd committed the unpardonable sin. He had taken off his helmet.

Paul says to put on the breastplate of faith and love, which guards your heart and conscience against accusation, and the helmet of the hope of salvation, which guards your mind. Your salvation is secure; Jesus paid for it all. Wear that assurance, and the enemy's darts lose their power.

text: You can't stop birds flying over your head, but you can stop them nesting in your hair. Don't own every thought.
explanation:
Scripture says the devil put it into Judas' heart to betray Jesus, and Satan filled Ananias' heart to lie. The enemy can throw thoughts at you, and he speaks in the first person: "I'm an addict." "I'm worthless." "I should jump." So you assume they're yours, and that ownership is what lets them settle in.

When a dark or blasphemous thought flies through your mind, it doesn't define you. Say, "That's not me. That's not my thought." Refuse to own it, and it has nowhere to land. Ask God for the gift of ignoring the enemy's suggestions and recognising His thoughts toward you, thoughts of good.

text: "Enlarge the place of your tent… lengthen your cords." Start planning for the healthy, blessed future God has for you.
explanation:
A friend in Israel had been diagnosed with a rare, aggressive bladder cancer, with about a 20% chance of survival even with treatment. He was downcast, seeing only darkness ahead. The word for him was Isaiah 54, which comes right after the cross in Isaiah 53: "Enlarge the place of your tent… lengthen your cords… for you shall expand to the right and to the left."

He was told: "Start planning your trips. Start seeing yourself well." He kept taking Communion, and the doctors later found no trace of cancer. Some will say, "Don't raise people's hopes." But a believer's hope stands on the finished work of Christ.

text: "My flesh also will rest in hope." Jesus' body lay in the tomb resting in hope, and it never saw decay.
explanation:
David prophesied of the Messiah: "My heart is glad… my flesh also will rest in hope. For You will not leave my soul in Sheol, nor will You allow Your Holy One to see corruption." Peter quoted it on Pentecost about Jesus' resurrection. Even His body, in the grave, rested in confident expectation.

Your body is the only house you'll live in on this earth. Don't abuse it with overwork, overeating or no rest. And let your flesh rest in hope too: hope of healing now, and of a resurrection body to come. Because He lives, decay doesn't have the final word.
